title: Fidelity Benchmark Campaign and Pricing Sensitivity Brief
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This brief defines a cross-functional campaign to: (1) run a structured fidelity benchmarking program across representative developer workloads, (2) measure fidelity vs. unit-cost sensitivity, and (3) generate packaging/pricing guidance and feature rollouts informed by measured economics. The goal is to produce prescriptive recommendations for Optimize/Conductor advisors, onboarding defaults, and pricing experiments for Q3–Q4 2027.

Why this matters:
- Customers trade off cost and result fidelity; we need repeatable, measurable guidance to surface sensible defaults and commercial levers.
- Provides evidence for fidelity-based SKU design, crediting rules, and fallback behaviors.
- Powers product telemetry and UX (Console advisors, preflight checks, cost estimators).

Scope and success criteria:
- Scope: hosted and dedicated serving tiers; text generation and chat; representative embeddings pipelines. Excludes on-prem private packaging and niche multimodal models for this phase.
- Success criteria (30-day):
  1. Complete benchmarking across 6 developer cohorts (see "Cohort Matrix") with quality and cost measurements.
  2. Produce 3 priced fidelity skus (Low/Medium/High) with modeled customer impact curves.
  3. Instrument Console advisor and cost estimator for rollout experiment.

Cohort Matrix (representative workloads):
1) Search reranking (short prompts, high throughput)
2) Conversational assistant (session state; context window 2–8 turns)
3) Document summarization (long context 4k–32k tokens)
4) Code generation (creative-to-deterministic mix)
5) Embeddings for semantic search (batched vectors)
6) Transactional microservices (low-latency constraints)

Measurement plan (what we measure):
- Quality metrics (per cohort): BLEU/ROUGE for summarization, MRR/NDCG for reranking, ROUGE/ROUGE-L for summarization, pass@k for code, embedding cosine recall@k. Also: developer-facing metrics (latency p50/p95), request error rate, token consumption breakdown.
- Economic metrics: cost-per-1M-input-tokens, cost-per-response, normalized cost-per-quality-point.
- Observability: correlation of latency and fidelity mode, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and GPU utilization per profile.

Telemetry and instrumentation (required fields):
Include the following telemetry keys in evaluation runs and production experiments:
- run_id (uuid)
- cohort (string)
- model_variant (string)
- fidelity_mode (low|medium|high|adaptive)
- avg_latency_ms_p50 (number)
- avg_latency_ms_p95 (number)
- tokens_input (int)
- tokens_output (int)
- cost_estimate_cents (number)
- quality_score (float)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (float)
- batch_size_mean (float)
- gpu_util_pct (float)

Example telemetry JSON (for evaluator ingestion):
{
  "run_id": "f8b2c12e-7b2e-4b9a-a6c2-9f6f8e26a2b1",
  "cohort": "conversational-assistant",
  "model_variant": "rw-v3-medium-quant",
  "fidelity_mode": "medium",
  "avg_latency_ms_p50": 85.2,
  "avg_latency_ms_p95": 210.6,
  "tokens_input": 12450,
  "tokens_output": 3200,
  "cost_estimate_cents": 46.2,
  "quality_score": 0.83,
  "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.42,
  "batch_size_mean": 8.1,
  "gpu_util_pct": 67.3
}

Design constraints and guardrails:
- Fidelity modes must be implementable as composable runtime flags (quantization profile + attention kernel choice + caching policy).
- No fidelity mode should increase p95 latency by >25% for transactional cohort unless explicitly marketed.
- Quality regressions must be detectable by shadow-eval harness with a defined rollback threshold (quality_score drop >= 0.05 normalized points).

Pricing sensitivity model (summary table):
Scenario | Workload | Mode | Mode cost delta | Expected quality delta
--- | --- | --- | ---: | ---:
Baseline (rw-v3-high) | Conversational | High | $0.00 / 1M tokens | quality 1.00
Quantized Medium | Conversational | Medium | -$240 / 1M tokens | quality 0.95
Aggressive Low | Conversational | Low | -$720 / 1M tokens | quality 0.87
Adaptive (slo-aware) | Conversational | Adaptive | -$150 / 1M tokens (estimated) | quality 0.93

Notes: dollar figures are estimated unit economics relative to baseline for GPU amortized costs and do not include margin or infra overhead. Final pricing will fold in network, storage, and Console feature costs.

Decision checkpoints and rollout plan:
1. Benchmarking sprint (2 weeks): run all cohorts through Low/Medium/High modes; collect telemetry and evaluations. Ownership: Applied ML & Evals (lead: Marco Ruiz).
2. Analysis (1 week): compute normalized cost-per-quality and run sensitivity curves; draft SKU proposals. Ownership: Product analytics (Aisha).
3. Pilot pricing experiment (4 weeks): select 4 pilot customers across size/vertical to validate UX and commercial response. Ownership: GTM (Samir Gupta) + Account teams.
4. Console integration (2 weeks parallel): add Advisor card showing recommended fidelity and cost delta with "Apply" flow. Ownership: Eng Developer Experience.
5. Release & A/B (8 weeks): run A/B test comparing current defaults vs. fidelity-sku defaults; track retention, spend churn, quality incidents. Ownership: Go-to-market + Product.

Rollout checklist:
- [ ] Benchmark data ingested into analytics store (schema validated)
- [ ] Shadow-eval alerts wired to regression slack channel (#fidelity-regressions)
- [ ] Console advisor UI implemented with cost-estimate calculator
- [ ] Pricing experiments configured in billing test environment
- [ ] Customer pilot consent and success criteria documented

SLOs and thresholds (per-cohort recommended):
- Transactional microservices: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, error_rate < 0.1%
- Conversational assistant: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, quality_score >= 0.88 for Medium mode
- Embeddings: throughput >= 2000 vectors/sec per GPU, recall@10 >= 0.92 for Medium mode

Billing and packaging guidance (draft):
- Introduce three optional fidelity add-ons for Optimize customers: "Fidelity Lite", "Fidelity Standard", "Fidelity Premium". Each maps to Low/Medium/High runtime flags and corresponding credit multipliers.
- Offer a trial period where first 100k tokens of any fidelity change are charged at baseline rates for pilot customers.
- For Dedicated customers, provide a "maintenance credit" for switching to Low mode to encourage trial, applied as a % discount on reserved monthly commit.

Example CLI (developer sandbox):
# run benchmark harness
redwood-cli benchmark run --cohort conversational --model rw-v3 --modes low,medium,high --out /tmp/bench-results.json

# estimate cost for a given prompt set
redwood-cli cost estimate --input /tmp/bench-prompts.json --model-variant rw-v3-medium-quant --fidelity medium

Security, compliance, and data handling:
- Evaluation runs must not include customer PII unless explicitly consented and covered under data-processing addendum (DPA).
- All telemetry used for pricing decisions must be stored in the internal analytics tier with restricted access and audit logs.

- Sensitivity curves: cost-per-quality plots with 90% confidence intervals
